extraction.name: MathQA
extraction.description: A large-scale dataset of math word problems and an interpretable neural math problem solver
extraction.creator: Aida Amini, Saadia Gabriel, Shanchuan Lin, Rik Koncel-Kedziorski, Yejin Choi, and Hannaneh Hajishirzi
extraction.publisher: University of Washington, Allen Institute for AI
extraction.citeAs: Amini et al. (2019). MathQA: Towards Interpretable Math Word Problem Solving with Operation-Based Formalisms.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The MathQA dataset consists of 37,200 math word problems, corresponding lists of multiple-choice options, and aligned operation programs. The problems are collected from the AQuA dataset and carefully annotated with formal operation programs using a dynamic annotation platform.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data collection is based on the AQuA dataset, which provides over 100K GRE- and GMAT-level math word problems.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The data preprocessing protocol involves categorizing math problems into math domains using term frequencies and then annotating those problems with formal operation programs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The annotation protocol involves using a dynamic annotation platform to align problems with operation programs. Annotators iteratively select operations and arguments until the problem is solved.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A dynamic annotation platform designed to provide basic math knowledge to annotators, iteratively calculate intermediate results, and employ quality control strategies.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotation analysis involves validating the quality of the annotated programs by checking whether the problems and annotated programs are aligned or not.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is available at https://math-qa.github.io/math-QA/ and will be updated with new annotations and problem categories.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset has the potential to improve the performance and interpretability of math word problem solvers, which can have a positive social impact on education and problem-solving.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may contain biases due to the noise in the AQuA dataset and the limitations of the representation language.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has limitations in terms of the types of math problems it covers and the complexity of the problems.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset can be used for training and testing math word problem solvers, as well as for evaluating the performance of different models.
